title: Shopify setup: connect the operations
summary: Define products, orders and market rules before themes and apps.
why: A finished storefront still needs correct payments, fulfillment and refunds.
Consistent data definitions reduce inventory, pricing and order errors.
know: SKUs/variants identify sellable units. Assign sources of truth for products, inventory and orders; prevent conflicting ERP/3PL writes.
Markets determine language, currency, pricing, availability, tax, payment and shipping. The merchant’s specialists confirm tax and legal rules.
Use native features first. Verify checkout, API and Markets capabilities for the current plan before adding apps.
inputs: Product samples, SKU/inventory sources, historical orders and customer needs
Markets, payment/shipping, returns, tax and operating owners
actions: Define product fields and a market matrix with field-level sources of truth.
Propose the theme, apps and integrations with costs, permissions and removal options.
Test payment success/failure, shipping/tax, discounts, stockouts, partial refunds/returns, restocking and notifications. Include excluded delivery addresses for bulky goods.
done: Sample orders match approved amounts, currencies, shipping and tax rules.
Inventory, orders and events agree; test data does not enter reported production revenue.
pitfalls: Treating successful tax configuration as legal compliance.
Adding overlapping apps without data ownership.
decision: The merchant approves markets, policies, taxes and costs; tests must match those rules.

reader.concept: Shopify manages commerce operations: products, orders, payments and inventory. Setup must establish how each transaction is handled.
reader.when: Use this for new stores, store handoffs, new markets or logistics integrations.

example.situation: A customer pays successfully, but shipping cost and inventory are wrong.
example.lesson: Test product, pricing, payment, logistics and inventory rules together.

reader.first_step: Trace a representative product from listing through shipping and refund.
terms: An internal code for a sellable item.
A specific product option combination, such as size and color.
